calls_unanswered.snippet:
Horrible communication and execution - This company responded to a home warranty repair claim for a pool salt cell generator.  The initial service call was 5/5.  The tech that responded had no idea what he was looking at or for, and I walked him through the fact that the SCG was not working and that I had trouble shot it to confirm.  After completing his tests, it was confirmed.  He advised I would get the same (comparable item - Pentair branded btw) and left.  Weeks went by with not follow up, return calls or emails from this vendor.  Calls go to a call center and even when marked urgent they do not call back.  Finally get a email that parts are on order - get a text on 5/18 to provide times they can come which I gave them 3 different days.  No response.  Multiple calls and emails  and a follow up with the HW Company, I finally get a text on 5/28 and the tech shows up with parts that a knowledgeable vendor would have came with.  The company could have directly replaced this SCG with the newer version of the model I had - unscrewed two unions, put in the new one and tightened, plugged in and left.  Instead, they bought a knock off Aqualix part from Amazon, destroyed the pool plumbing that was actually done by a pool company. frontline_communication.snippet:
Horribly bad experience. Originally scheduled cleaning with them beginning of July since they were contracted with AHS. Unfortunately, AC went out night before appointment. The individual that came out gave me a quote for the new ac system (handler and compressor). Stated it wasn't worth filing with AHS as they wouldn't cover it anyway. He said they'd give me a $500 AHS credit that they offer on new units (later found out that AHS doesn't do this and have never heard of it).

They were able to come out next day to begin work. Upon arriving they informed me that the air handler in the attic had to be relocated, that it wasn't serviceable in the attic and had to be relocated to the garage. This was going to cost me another $700 at which point I pushed back and they said they'd eat the cost. Oddly enough the materials they needed to relocate the unit were already dropped off in the morning, prior to telling me it would need to be relocated. During the installation I told them, and texted the salesperson, that they were blocking the garage light and door switches. I was told this was installed to code.

They completed the installation around July 7th at which point they still had to replace breakers in the panel to accommodate the new units. In addition, they had left work trash in two boxes that I told them was fine assuming it would be picked up within a couple days. Needless to say, it took multiple calls and emails and nearly 2 weeks before the trash was removed and breakers replaced. Nearly a month after the installation was completed an inspector arrived and failed the installation.

The inspection failed because of improper scope of work on the permit, relocating the unit, not installing a bollard in front of the unit, not installing a protective covering around the duct at ground level. Not surprisingly it was also failed due to blocking the switches. Because they relocated the unit and had to redo electrical they also required an electrical inspection which was never scheduled.

Another week has passed and I was contacted by the contractor that someone would be out the next day to complete the work noted by the inspector. At 10am, the next day, I called them concerned that they wouldn't be able to complete the work in time and that as a result we wouldn't have ac for the night. They apologized for the miscommunication and that I was misinformed, that they wouldn't be completing the work. They were only sending someone out to come up with a plan to move the unit. They also didn't have the parts in stock yet.

To be continued because they still haven't completed the work and inspections are still not complete.

The level of miscommunication, inability to listen and their lack of follow through is beyond unacceptable. These folks shouldn't be trusted with your ac and the fact that they failed an inspection for 4 things on a single installation is terrible.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer was told work would be completed and then given contradictory information, an explicit miscommunication.
frontline_communication.quote: They apologized for the miscommunication and that I was misinformed, that they wouldn't be completing the work

service_quality_in_session.snippet: My well pump froze during the the last freeze we had. I had already done some research online to see if I could fix the issue. What I found online was it could be my pressure switch, pressure gauge, or my check valve. I replaced my pressure switch and it did not correct the issue. My pressure gauge was reading that it had pressure, so I didn't replace that. I called AND Service to set up a service call. I was told someone would be out in 2 to 4 hours. It was at the 6 hour time mark that the tech showed up. The tech asked how old my pump was, I told him it had been replaced last year. At that point, he just told me to have the pump replaced because it would still be under warranty. T is not under warranty, as he sssumed. I then asked him if it could be the pressure guage that was the problem. He said that it was reading pressure, so it was still good. At no time did he do anything other than walk around my pump. He didn't check anything and never asked for the pump to be turned on. I bought a new pump and installed it. Replace the pressure guage and everything.  The old pressure guage that he said was accurate is no longer attached to anything and is reading 35 psi. Overall, it was waiting 6 hours to be told just to replace the pump because it is under warranty, without checking anything.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I am writing to formally document a highly unprofessional and unsafe experience with Integrity Home Solutions.

Integrity Home Solutions was dispatched to an Airbnb property I manage to assess a defective light switch. They provided a quote of $750 to replace the switch, which was approximately $500 higher than my next highest quote. I informed them that we would be proceeding with another company.

Shortly afterward, I received a guest review stating that electrical wiring was exposed and unsafe for children. I immediately went to the property to investigate and discovered that the exposed wiring was from the same light switch Integrity Home Solutions had evaluated. The switch had been removed from the wall and left with all wiring exposed, creating a serious safety hazard.

When I contacted Integrity Home Solutions to address this issue, I was initially told that I would be charged a fee to have the light switch returned to the condition it was in when they arrived. After approximately 45 minutes on the phone, the fee was finally removed.

Leaving exposed electrical wiring in a home—especially one used by paying guests and families—is not only dangerous but completely unacceptable. This situation reflects a serious lapse in professionalism, safety standards, and customer care.

I would strongly caution others against using Integrity Home Solutions based on this experience.

Portable dehumidifier is the our best friend now.

Did purchase this system for increased level of comfort, but so far even level of comfort provided by “regular” A/C system is not reachable.

ARS refuses to admit the problem and to open case with the manufacturer - Carrier

Both my bathrooms smell like damp

It is harder to breathe inside the home than outdoor when I coming home from work because of the humidity level inside.

Another issue on an already lengthy list of problems is that the AC unit wastes my money by unnecessarily utilizing electric heating rather than the more efficient heat pump mode. The display merely states "heat pump locked out," providing no explanation or resolution.

This is undoubtedly the worst air conditioning system I've ever encountered.

I recently had my air conditioner replaced, and I couldn't be happier with the results! The new unit works efficiently, keeping my home cool and comfortable. I won't be calling them again, but if you get Tony you are blessed, he doesn't say much but sometimes that's all you need. Tony reminds me of him but he didnt say he was him, its been years so i just spoke well of the first tech in case he was him, he stayed quiet, anywho, good salt of the earth folks though. booking_friction.snippet:
Honest review of my recent experience: I signed up for their "Gold Membership" which includes 2 maintenance visits. The experience was pleasant to start as the staff was very friendly and quick to get my first appointment scheduled. Unfortunately, it took a turn from here on out. They provided me a 4-hour window in which I took off work for. The technician never showed up and was I contacted to reschedule. The tech showed up on the second visit and after inspecting my unit (less than 1 year old), showed me that there was "growth" in both units and attempted to sell me on ~$5k UV light system. He then went on to tell me that he could not clean out the growth as it is not included with my package. After he left, I found my brand new carpet (picture below) covered in dirt. I contacted the office to give them a chance to rectify the situation as I had to rent a carpet cleaner just to get it out, and was told the service manager was out and would get back to me. I followed up a week later and once again was told they would follow up with me. It's now been a month and I haven't heard back.

Overall, I would not recommend using this company for their annual HVAC maintenance based on this experience. I essentially paid $265 to have someone come out and tell me my unit was dirty and then stain my carpet.

calls_unanswered.snippet: I had Mario’s come out because they installed our AC system in our new build home 5 years ago. The system was cooling but it was very humid in the house. The tech who came out told me my system wasn’t designed to remove humidity from the house and would need a whole new, higher end system to do that (removing humidity and creating cold air in the house are literally the only functions of every air conditioner, so this was a bold lie). After telling me my system was running perfectly fine the tech offered to install a $2800 uv bulb to stop any mold growth due to the house being humid. Not sure who is paying near $3k for a light bulb. The tech then offered to clean my drain pan and condensate line (which would not do away with the $110 house call), for a grand total of over $450, please save your money and do this yourself it is not hard in any capacity. I had to diagnose the issue myself after the tech left and found that my blower fan would not stop running, even if I turned off the whole system. This pushes the water from the evaporator coils back in the house, making it humid. My system was still under warranty for parts so I called Mario’s the next day to see what their labor rates were. The girl who answered told me she would have the manager call me, surprise, he never did. This outfit is your typical upsell whatever they can without actually fixing your issue. They avoided a 1 star review by at least being nice.

hidden_subcontracting.snippet: Buyer beware!!! My HVAC was weak, unable to keep up with the heat in July. I have a Homeowners warranty,  I called them to put in a service request, and Comfort Pro was called out the next day. I have never heard of this company. They seemed Professional. I was quickly told I needed a new system. I agreed, as I already knew that my unit was 11 years old, and it was underrated for the size of the house. I told them I was looking for a high-efficiency unit. I was offered a quote, and I accepted with hesitation due to the cost; the tech used the tariffs as an excuse. I was told it can be done the same day. That was a surprise. I should have stopped at that point, but I needed Cool air. My house was over 80 degrees as my old system was struggling to keep up. I accepted the offer. Two hours later, a Spanish-speaking gentleman arrived by himself, and another gentleman was on the phone. He was translating for him, asking me to allow him to start, and he would be there shortly. I asked if the tech was capable of starting, and he assured me he was; I should have stopped again at that point. It turns out they sub their installs out. All red flags. He started the removal process and and it took the other guy 3 hours before he arrived, Long story short- they took 11 hours to remove and install a new unit, the next day the unit was still runing as I woke to 65 degrees in the house, the tech had bypassed the thermostat just to get me cool air as he did not know what he was doing to wire the thermostat, it was 11 pm when he completed. I called the office, and they sent another tech out as I had to shut the system down. While I was checking the job, I noticed my laminate flooring was scarred due to the tech not putting any kind of cloth or cover to protect my flooring. I took pictures and showed the tech when he arrived. I received a quote for the repair of my flooring and sent it to the company. I was offered a soft start instead of replacing my flooring. I was livid. I should have been given the soft start due to the unit contacts banging when it turns on, and for the cost I paid for it, I was assured it was quieter than my older unit. I did not accept the offer. I have not, at the time of writing this review, had my flooring repaired. Please beware of my warning. The company has been nothing but trouble from the start.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Technicians came out and made proper diagnosis of my AC problem. However, they did not bother (or call their office) to tell me all the parts were still under warranty and presented me with two options, including a brand new unit for $12k (the unit is less than 4 years old). I looked up the serial # and confirmed it is covered by Johnson Controls/York.

Second and third opinions from other local providers confirmed the unit is in pristine shape and the faulty components are under manufacture original warranty and their quotes will save me almost 80% from what I was quoted on site. To even think that suggesting a brand new unit purchase when the current one is less than 5 years old is very concerning  especially given that suffering from lack of AC is a desperate situation here in Florida. Even their quote for a replacement compressor was 4k more than what I am able to find from others.

30 minutes later- as I was getting ready to leave the home for the weekend- the technician came back to tell me what the service fee would be for their visit. Had I left the house and not noticed the van still parked down the street I would not have been made aware of the $ amount owed for their visit). The  process was unprofessional and disorganized- however the back office folks including Amy were very pleasant to deal with and thank her for helping me out.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Staff withheld material information (active warranty coverage) that other providers later confirmed.
frontline_communication.quote: they did not bother (or call their office) to tell me all the parts were still under warranty

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
It is nice to have a large company and to let everyone know how great you are. I thought things were progressing nicely. I agreed to purchase a system using their 36 month no interest financing but unfortunately I was not approved despite 700 + credit scores. The Representative told me that if I could get my own financing he could schedule it if I put $1000 down. So that is what I did. I was not able to get the financing that I needed but the representative never told me I would be on the hook for the permits if the deal did not go through. I feel that there should be more disclosure and they certainly should not leave the customer at risk by moving forward with a deal that was not sealed. I am very disappointed with Universal Air and Heat and would not recommend to family and friends. Additionally the Rep was to arrive between 10 and 2 and never showed up until after 3 with no courtesy call advising of the delay. Upon checking his paper work he found that he did not even have the right telephone number. Just an unfortunate experience overall.

PLEASE NOTE THAT SINCE THE ORIGINAL REVIEW, THE COMPANY RESOLVED THE MATTER TO MY SATISFACTION IN A TIMELY MANNER AND I WOULD CONSIDER USING THEM FOR MY AC REPLACEMENT PROJECT SHOULD THE NEED ARISE.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Undisclosed permit cost left the customer with an unexpected charge when financing fell through.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: the representative never told me I would be on the hook for the permits if the deal did not go through

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet: I hate leaving bad reviews, but when it's severely warranted, it's important to. I was a previous customer of Total Air and used their subscription to maintain my units, after a 2 unnecessarily high quotes for repair, I ended my subscription and moved to another company. After a couple of years, I re-contacted Total Air for a quote on a new AC unit, and again, they came in substantially over the cost of every other quote I received. After that, they called me with an offer to inspect my units, and provide a cleaning, seemingly as a win back strategy to earn my business back. I accepted, and when finished, was presented with a bill that surpassed what I have paid in the past, and the only option being to sign up for their recurring subscription again. After another two months I call and asked to cancel the subscription. Lori, from accounting called me with a balance. That's fine, but I do reserve the right to review, and submit payment. Lori asked (rudely lol) to use the card on file, I said no, and she submitted the payment despite my request not to. Note, this was not an overdue payment. I simply asked to receive the invoice via email, which she did, then immediately sent me a receipt of payment. Lori has yet to return my call. It's all a bit weird, but reinforced my distaste for the company.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: A win-back inspection/cleaning offer ended in an unexpectedly large bill plus forced subscription.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: was presented with a bill that surpassed what I have paid in the past

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
1. The wrong condensing unit was installed—a Merit instead of the Elite model specified in my contract. If I hadn’t checked the unit’s tag myself, this expensive mistake would have gone unnoticed for the unit’s entire lifespan. Although the correct unit was eventually installed, no explanation was ever given for the error. Caveat emptor.
2. After installation, my credit card was charged multiple times for the $15,200 cost. I had to call Hale’s office repeatedly to reverse the extra charges. No one explained why this happened, and it was only resolved because I followed up myself.
3. For a month after installation, I called every few days requesting an invoice listing the installed equipment’s model and serial numbers, along with a copy of the permit, to apply for a Duke Energy rebate. This simple request proved difficult. After a month of persistence, I received an invoice without serial numbers. I eventually found the permit online myself. The office seems unable to handle non-routine requests or follow through accurately.
4. After a month, I called three times asking for management to contact me regarding these issues and the installation itself. No one ever got back to me.
5. Permitting was complicated by two major hurricanes in Fall 2024, requiring a permitting official to visit my home multiple times due to repeated inspection failures. The last failure was due to the technician not checking a box on the AHU sticker indicating the heat strip type. It would have been helpful to be notified when installation was approved, as requested—I wrongly assumed it was. About a month ago, I received a letter from the City of Seminole stating the permit had expired and the installer might be reported to the state licensing office. I informed Hale's, and only then did they arrange for the permitting official to return and finalize the inspection—well over a year after the initial installation. This would not have happened if I hadn’t reported the letter.
6. In December, I was called to renew my service contract on all three systems in my home (all installed by Hale’s), but the free preventive maintenance contract offered with the new unit was not honored. Neither I nor the representative could explain why. I pointed out that the new unit didn’t require maintenance yet, and was still under warranty. I asked to have someone check with management and respond, but received no follow-up.
7. More recently, after voicemails about owing money for preventive maintenance, I called again and learned that Hale’s wanted to charge me in advance for this year’s maintenance on all three systems. The person I spoke to—who had previously promised to look into the free maintenance—had no record of our earlier conversation, and still couldn’t answer my question. I decided not to continue servicing my units with Hale’s and informed them.

booking_friction.snippet:
I used to recommend Beach Air when they were locally owned. They were always fair, reasonably priced, and easy to work with. Unfortunately, my most recent experience after they were bought out (along with Waccamaw Heating & Air) was completely different.
I called because my unit was going into low pressure lockout. The technician looked at it for maybe 10 minutes and told me it had a leak. He said a pressure test would cost $700, evacuation and recharge of 7 lbs of refrigerant would be $1,400, and depending on what was leaking the repair could range anywhere from $100 to $4,000 — if it was even repairable. He also strongly suggested that since the unit is 10 years old, I should just replace the entire system.
When I declined replacement, he told me I’d have to schedule the pressure test and they were booked weeks out. With the cold weather we were having, I couldn’t wait.
I decided to investigate myself. I filled my nitrogen tank for $42 and as soon as I removed the service port caps, I could hear refrigerant leaking from the valve cores — something the technician should have easily noticed. I replaced both valve cores for $0.28 total. I pressure tested at 300 PSI overnight and the system held perfectly, confirming that was the only leak. I then vacuumed and recharged the system, and it has been working great ever since.
For comparison, I purchased 25 lbs of refrigerant for $200. Being quoted $1,400 for 7 lbs is excessive. Even more frustrating, when this company was locally owned, I paid around $300 for an evacuation and recharge.
On top of that, the technician argued with me that they “don’t work with home warranty companies and never have,” which is simply not true — they handled my warranty claims in the past and received payment directly from the warranty company.
Either this technician didn’t know what he was doing, or he was trying to upsell a major repair or full system replacement that wasn’t necessary. What turned out to be a simple valve core replacement could have cost me thousands — potentially $10,000+ for a new unit — had I followed their recommendation.
I won’t be calling them again and will be looking for another locally owned HVAC company. Very disappointed in how far they’ve fallen.
booking_friction.reasoning: Customer needed a pressure test during cold weather but the next available appointment was weeks away.

frontline_communication.snippet:
We were contacted and informed that our current A/C service provider had been acquired and that your company would now be handling our service. Based on that representation, we scheduled an appointment.

On the day of service, I received a message requesting to move the appointment earlier due to staffing issues. I was initially unable to accommodate but ultimately adjusted my schedule. Despite this, the technician still arrived significantly later than the agreed time.

Upon arrival, the technician stated he could not perform the service because we were under contract with another company—the same company we were told had been acquired. I subsequently contacted them directly and confirmed that they have not been purchased and remain fully operational.

This situation was highly misleading and raises serious concerns about your business practices. When I called for clarification, your representative backtracked and attempted to place responsibility on us, which was both unprofessional and unacceptable.

I would strongly advise others to verify any such claims before scheduling service.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Company gave misleading/contradictory information about being acquired, an unclear-information communication failure.
frontline_communication.quote: This situation was highly misleading and raises serious concerns about your business practices.

frontline_communication.snippet:
If you’re looking for a Tampa-based company with strong customer service that truly goes above and beyond, Bayside Heating & Air is not it. This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever had.

They lock you into a three-year agreement, and once you’re signed up, you’re stuck dealing with ongoing issues. I’ve had repeated problems with their technicians. In one instance, a technician got insulation throughout my air handler, which then blew into my home for weeks. Customer service initially denied any mistake, but even the technicians they later sent out to clean the ductwork admitted the issue was caused by improper work.

More recently, the paneling on my air handler started deteriorating, with the foil peeling off. Instead of properly repairing it with foil tape, they removed it entirely, leaving insulation exposed. This has now created moisture issues and a musty smell throughout my home.

When I reached out again, customer service was rude and unwilling to take responsibility. There is simply no accountability here. Overall, extremely disappointing experience.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Explicit complaint about rude tone from customer service staff.
frontline_communication.quote: customer service was rude and unwilling to take responsibility

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but homeowners deserve to hear this. I built a multi-million-dollar custom home and worked with many contractors throughout the project. I had absolutely no issues with any contractor except Cox Heating & Air.

Cox installed four HVAC systems totaling over $70,000. Three performed well. The fourth never worked correctly due to Cox’s installation choices — including mounting the outdoor unit higher than the indoor air handler (preventing proper drainage) and installing unnecessary dual filtration that restricted airflow.

After months of discussion, Cox acknowledged the issue stemmed from their own workmanship and agreed to absorb the $500 charge for the condensate pump required only because of their installation error.

Despite that agreement, Cox later sent the written-off amount to a debt collector, who then contacted not just us but also my husband’s parents, who have nothing to do with this project. This was distressing and entirely inappropriate.

To be clear: the dollar amount was never the issue. In a project of this scale, $500 is less than a rounding error to me. This was always about principle, professionalism, and accountability. Unfortunately, Cox was the only contractor on my entire multi-million-dollar build who did not uphold those standards.

I recommend homeowners proceed with caution.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Customer was sent to collections for a charge the company had already agreed to absorb — unexpected billing after the fact.

service_quality_in_session.snippet:
⭐☆☆☆☆ ABSOLUTELY UNACCEPTABLE SERVICE, THEY DESERVE NO STARS !!
My wife and I experienced one of the worst customer service encounters we have ever had with an HVAC company.  This is terrible !
Technician Daryl arrived with an attitude and appeared more concerned about getting to his next appointment than properly diagnosing our AC issue. Calling me Bro instead of calling me Sir i knew i was in for a real unprofessional technician that was sent to my home.
We repeatedly asked simple questions  to Daryl about water leaking from the system and received no clear explanation. Instead of investigating the problem thoroughly, he became argumentative, defensive, and dismissive. We never had scene a AC company so unprofessional .
What makes this situation even worse is that the service call was never properly completed. Daryl did not inspect the entire system,  Nor he did not check the attic unit, did not perform a comprehensive diagnosis, and made no effort to access all components that should have been examined.
Daryl  made no effort to retrieve a ladder and perform a complete evaluation. When we continued asking reasonable questions about our AC system, he became frustrated with simple questions from us and  kept stating lhow he had 17years of experience and he knew what he was talking about . Later we found out after a major complaint to his office he lied and only had 4 years of experience.
Rather than troubleshoot the problem, Daryl Max Cools  top experience technician repeatedly insisted everything was fine while refusing to provide simple  answers that made sense.
The interaction became so confrontational that Daryl abruptly announced he was leaving before completing the inspection. As paying customers, we were left with unanswered questions, an unresolved issue, and no confidence that our system had been properly evaluated.
When I later spoke with management, including Jason, I found the same lack of accountability and professionalism. Instead of addressing our concerns and ensuring a proper inspection was completed, management appeared more interested in defending the technician than resolving the problem.
An HVAC company is hired to diagnose problems, explain findings, and treat customers with respect. In our experience, Max Cool failed on all three counts. We were treated as though our questions were an inconvenience rather than legitimate concerns from homeowners seeking answers.
If you value professionalism, thorough service, communication, and respect, I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere. Based on our experience, this was a complete waste of time , waste of money and one of the most frustrating service calls we have ever encountered.
Stay away !!
Consumer beware!!
service_quality_in_session.reasoning: Technician rushed the visit, skipped inspecting the attic unit, and left before completing the inspection.
service_quality_in_session.quote: appeared more concerned about getting to his next appointment than properly diagnosing our AC issue

I decided to text the number today and the owner, Channing, is stating that there is nothing that they can do.  Added photo of dryer vent cleaning tool, which could have caused a house fire. Terrible customer service and extremely unprofessional handling of a simple service. A technician came out to give a dryer vent cleaning estimate. I called a handyman, who discovered that a dryer vent cleaning tool had been left stuck inside my vent, which is a serious fire hazard. I called this company three times and left messages — no one ever returned my calls. I had to hire another company to remove the tool and inspect the vent, and I’m now stuck with a $300 bill for a dryer that worked perfectly before their technician touched it. I am still waiting for a supervisor or the owner to contact me.

No accountability, no follow-up, and no concern for safety or the customer. I would not recommend this company to anyone.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
The good: I had my ac repaired by Dave (who was experienced and super pleasant to talk to) and Rob was very responsive to my after hours call.

The bad: I read the reviews on yelp and they were not sounding good at all, but them I read the google reviews and decided to go for it (please read the yelp reviews if you are considering this company). So they fixed my contacter. Afterwards, my neighbor asked his ac guy what a contacter costs and he said around 150 and that is consistent with what I've researched as well, so I reached out to Rob just to inquire if the 350 portion of my bill was just the part or if it was also labor (because I also paid the 99.00 diagnostic fee, and he diagnosed the problem within the first thirty minutes - there was an issue with finding my unit on the roof but that time was not counted against me). So the actual labor once he found my correct unit was very minimal, maybe 15 minutes max.

In response, Rob said that the price was parts alone and that the 150.00 number sounded like the estimate for a single prong contactor. I said, "OK, so the 350 is more like the cost of a two prong" and he said yes, and that they also had to make a little money, which I understand that.

I ended up researching some more and discovered that the single and double prong are the same price and at that point I reached back out and very gently said I wouldn't be posting a bad review, that I'm not angry, I just don't like the fact that I was told that the 350 was largely the price of the part alone and I said that I wouldn't be a patron going forward.

And I still wasn't going to post a review but I can't sleep and I feel disturbed by how he responded. He kept saying in long texts that he didn't say what he said about the part price, and that they fixed the problem, he wasn't there, he didn't have the prices in front of him when when he told me the part price, that he wasn't the one to fix the ac, that the ac was fixed so why was I turning on him, that I was picking apart his every word, that he regretted checking in with me so often if I was now angry (I'm not angry), that he was just an employee abd they don't make the prices, gas prices are high, it takes a lot to run a business, and to enjoy my comfort. He said that multiple times. Enjoy your comfort. Felt very passive aggressive.

My impression is that he is very business minded and cares a lot about keeping his business reputation clear, however, the way he treated me, with passive aggressive remarks after very gently explaining why I won't be a returning patron, that revealed a lot.

So I'm posting my honest review so that I can stop thinking about this. Rob, I don't believe you are a bad guy at all. But I do feel disturbed by our interaction. I am grateful for you guys promptly coming out and fixing my contacter and as I said many times in response to you, I'm not angry. I felt the need to write this review to give others a clear picture of what they might experience and also to not gaslight myself, because I heard what I heard and even though you say you never said it about the part price, you absolutely did. And I repeated it multiple times so you could have corrected me if there was a misunderstanding. The prices are not the problem (although if I had gone with my neighbors ac guy it would've been tremendously cheaper, rather than going with an ac company - which I do regret). The problem is the dishonesty about the part price and the passive aggressive responses. When trust is broken, I'm out.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Non-transparent pricing: customer was told $350 was the part cost alone and later discovered that was misrepresented.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: The problem is the dishonesty about the part price

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I am renting a house with a newly-installed, almost $10,000 Airtemp A/C system, that has a 1-year, all-inclusive warranty on the parts and installation, according to the home-owner.

The system is only 7 months old and we've only had 2 issues.  One was the filter had to be replaced, so I bought a new one and we were good up until June 1, 2018.

My wife is 7 months pregnant and high-risk with a heart condition, so getting it addressed as quickly as possible is incredibly important for her health, so I called our property manager.  We did the some standard trouble-shooting, checked the filter and everything looked fine.

Our property manager called Florida Energy Air Conditioning Inc. to try and help us get them out here ASAP and apparently there was an altercation between him and the staff, not related to me, as I've only ever been exceptionally pleasant to the technicians who came out, Denise the office manager and even Cary, the owner of the company.  I even went so far as to praise how knowledgeable and friendly Denise and their technicians were when I worked with them personally, to Cary, and to Denise herself.

In their defense, we did call at a very inopportune time and they were extremely busy with other customers, but they sent 2 of their technicians out to look at the issue the next day anyway, after I called and spoke with Cary, who walked me through a couple of more advanced troubleshooting steps to see if we could get the system working again.

While talking to Cary on the phone, I went outside to check the outdoor unit and found that it was iced over.  Not only that, but the compressor inside of the unit was leaned over and resting against the copper reverse valve tubing inside of the unit.  I wasn't sure at the time, but I'm sure that the metal outer housing of the compressor should not be resting against a copper pipe as the vibrations from the compressor will eventually lead to damage to the copper piping and Cary agreed that the compressor should be perfectly up-right and not leaning at what appeared to be, approximately, a 30-degree angle and resting against the reverse-valve.

When the technicians arrived, they took the outer housing off of the outdoor unit, and climbed inside, and found that I was correct.  All of the freon leaked out where the compressor and reverse-valve were touching, creating a hole in the pipe where contact was made.  They tried to weld the pipe, twice, to fix it, but could not get the issue resolved and decided that the reverse-valve had to be replaced, which was a special-order part from one of their suppliers.  The part wouldn't arrive for 5 days.

Regardless, I understood that the company was busy and decided that we would do our best to deal with it by purchasing fans for the house to try and stay cool.  The technicians ordered the part and left.  After they left, I called Cary to see if there was any way to have the part over-nighted at my expense, which I did pay for, as a show of good faith.  Cary then told me that after the altercation between the property manager and Denise and he would no longer work with the property manager of the home.  He would only work with the home owner, but he said he'd look into having the part over-nighted and call me back.

I decided that I would take the higher ground and called Cary back and VERY nicely told him that I completely understood that they were busy and we would hold out until they could get on-site, to which he replied that the part could be sent over-night.

The issue was resolved the day the part arrived, but today I received a certified letter with an unpaid bill for $1060.00 for services related to what was OBVIOUSLY covered under warranty.  I shouldn't be involved as this is not my house, but even after speaking with Cary, he SPECIFICALLY told me that he knew, but he wants his money and he is just following the path of least resistance....ME...  STAY AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY.  This is between the home owner and the company, NOT ME.  This is EXTREMELY unprofessional, even after treating them all with the utmost respect

I’ve been waiting all day for a dishwasher repair that was scheduled almost a week out. Was originally told my window was 8am-12pm, then called around noon to check in and was told 2-3. It’s after three now and no one is answering my calls or responding to my texts. What a waste of my only day off. I’m furious. Should have looked at all the similar reviews first so I wouldn’t be shocked.

Follow up post-review response:
Not sure how finding you through my home warranty makes any difference, happy for you to explain to everyone reading these reviews how that matters.
Obviously our chances of doing any business are zero but as someone with 20 years of customer service experience and far better reviews for my businesses than you have I’d offer some advice.
1) Publicly disqualifying your potential clients due to what source they come from (ex warranty claims) is not a good look.
2) Taking no ownership whatsoever for failing to arrive at either time YOU confirmed for me is not going to lead you to success.
I’d have been fine with “today got too busy we’ll have to reschedule” or really any kind of communication. I think if you had been waiting all day for someone at your home that you had to chase down for any information, you’d be pretty frustrated too.
3) When there is a conflict, it never hurts to offer a solution if not for the business you’d earn with me, for your own reputation. You immediately gave up on even trying to reschedule.

I hope this helps, best of luck.

frontline_communication.snippet:
1 Star – Extremely Unprofessional and Unreliable Technician

This is by far one of the worst service experiences I’ve had through a home warranty company.

The technician assigned to my pool pump claim, Kent, never canceled his first appointment. I took a half day off work to be home, only to find out the same day—after I texted him asking if he accepted debit card or Zelle for the deductible—that he was not coming. He then said he would come within the next two days.

I asked him to formally notify Home Choice Warranty (HCW) of the change. He claimed he already had and blamed HCW for not informing me. When I called HCW to confirm, I was told he never contacted them to reschedule at all.

When he finally showed up on a date he personally chose, he inspected the pool pump and said it needed to be replaced because the motor bearings were worn out. At that time, the pump was running with an extremely loud noise. HCW later denied replacement because the pump was “still working,” even though the technician himself recommended replacement.

Less than ten days later, the pump completely failed. I requested a recall, and because it was a recall, the same technician was required to return. An appointment was automatically generated, but he never confirmed it and did not show up. When I contacted him, he vaguely said, “I will come at some point next week,” without giving a date.

HCW contacted him again, and he promised to come on Tuesday and contact me. He never contacted me and never showed up. On Wednesday, I texted him asking which of the remaining two days he planned to come—no response. When HCW contacted him again, he said he would not be able to come out for the next two weeks.

Due to his repeated no-shows and lack of professionalism, HCW was forced to reassign my claim.

It is also important to note that Kent operates under another company name, No Sweat Residential Services LLC, which is the company that accepted my claim through HCW.

My advice: stay away from this technician and this company. Unreliable, unprofessional, poor communication, and complete disregard for customers’ time. No homeowner should have to deal with this kind of service.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Technician gave the customer information that directly contradicted what the warranty company confirmed.
frontline_communication.quote: When I called HCW to confirm, I was told he never contacted them to reschedule at all

I was very impressed with how I was treated and how the job started to replace my central air unit.  Ken kept me updated and let me know exactly when it would be done.  After the unit was installed and was running on July 19, Ken said he would be back the next day to install the UV light and remove all the packing material, ie 2x4s, cardboard, insulation and wiring that was left in my garage.  I didn’t hear from him for a week and then learned that he had been sick.  I guess there was nobody else that could fill in for him.  I was then told it would be done on July 25th but nobody showed up nor did he notify me.  I contacted him by text on the 26th and he told me Rick couldn’t reach me even though I was home and didn’t receive any missed calls.  He said he would be out himself the next day, but again he didn’t come nor did he notify me.  I have now texted twice asking for an answer, and he has not responded.  Initially when he was selling me on his services the communication and customer service were great, however after the payment and install he dropped the ball and left me with an incomplete job and a pile of trash.  (Photo of trash in my garage posted). What started as a good working relationship has ended on a very sour note especially since I am 80 years old and able to move all the trash myself.

Since posting this, I have learned that this is a fraudulent company and has no affiliation with AC Allstars.  Ken Hart is his real name, not Ken Hunt like he told me.  I guess he changed his name, because he had been fired by the real AC Allstars company.  He did not pull a permit, and now I have had to hire another company, this time legitimate, to inspect the a/c and pull a permit in order to have a valid warranty.  I also learned from the real AC Allstars that this is not the first time Ken Hart has done this.  Beware, do not use this man’s services.

booking_friction.snippet:
I hired Happy Wife A/C for routine HVAC maintenance and ended up very disappointed with the experience overall.

The biggest problem was repeated missed appointments and poor communication. The owner Bryan told me several times that he would come out on specific dates/times, but he either showed up hours late, days late, or not at all. I had to constantly follow up to get an ETA or to find out if/when he was actually coming back to finish the job or check on issues with my system.

At one point, I came home and found that my system wasn’t running correctly—the compressor/condenser was not running when there was a call for cooling. I was told he would come back out yesterday to take a look, but he never showed and never contacted me to reschedule. At that point, I felt I had no choice but to hire another company to get the system working again.

To his credit, the original technician did note that there were burned high-voltage wires and a weak capacitor at the condenser and left the power off due to a potential fire hazard, which I appreciate. But the follow-through to actually resolve the situation and get my system reliably cooling again just didn’t happen, despite multiple promises and follow-ups on my end.  ￼

I ended up calling another company, who came out, diagnosed a bad defrost control board, and replaced it under warranty. After that, my system started working properly again.  ￼

Based on my experience, I would not use Happy Wife A/C again. If you do decide to hire them, I’d recommend getting clear, written appointment times and being prepared to follow up a lot—and double-check that your system is actually running correctly after the work is done.
booking_friction.reasoning: Repeated missed and slipped appointments made the job hard to schedule and confirm.

followup_dropped.snippet:
I hired Happy Wife A/C for routine HVAC maintenance and ended up very disappointed with the experience overall.

The biggest problem was repeated missed appointments and poor communication. The owner Bryan told me several times that he would come out on specific dates/times, but he either showed up hours late, days late, or not at all. I had to constantly follow up to get an ETA or to find out if/when he was actually coming back to finish the job or check on issues with my system.

At one point, I came home and found that my system wasn’t running correctly—the compressor/condenser was not running when there was a call for cooling. I was told he would come back out yesterday to take a look, but he never showed and never contacted me to reschedule. At that point, I felt I had no choice but to hire another company to get the system working again.

To his credit, the original technician did note that there were burned high-voltage wires and a weak capacitor at the condenser and left the power off due to a potential fire hazard, which I appreciate. But the follow-through to actually resolve the situation and get my system reliably cooling again just didn’t happen, despite multiple promises and follow-ups on my end.  ￼

I ended up calling another company, who came out, diagnosed a bad defrost control board, and replaced it under warranty. After that, my system started working properly again.  ￼

Based on my experience, I would not use Happy Wife A/C again. If you do decide to hire them, I’d recommend getting clear, written appointment times and being prepared to follow up a lot—and double-check that your system is actually running correctly after the work is done.
followup_dropped.reasoning: Customer chased a promised return visit that never came, forcing them to hire another company.

I was hesitant to remove my previous 5-star review to leave this new one, because working with Hometown Heating and Air initially started as a great experience with both service and customer service. After detecting an issue with my HVAC and waiting on a part that I was told was on backorder, they apparently stopped communicating with my warranty company. I feel that I was also misled because Hometown Heating and Air said that my claim was canceled by my warranty company and that it was my warranty company's responsibility to notify me. My warranty company confirmed that the claim was never canceled. My customer dashboard when I logged into my account also still showed the claim as active.

When I called Hometown Heating and Air to ask if they could pick-up the newer pending claim from my warranty company, I was told that they are very busy and that the earliest they could come back out to my condo would be in two weeks. I was more than okay with waiting because again, they were so wonderful to work with up to that point. After promising to call me back to schedule that follow-up, they have since went completely silent.

I truly wish Hometown Heating and Air had just been honest about not wanting to finish the repair so I could have moved on to another company sooner. I would have still left my previous 5-star review.

Living in Florida, if this HVAC issue had happened during the peak summer months, this lack of transparency would have been a truly miserable situation for me. Ghosting a customer who is loyal to a brand is not only unprofessional but saddening.
followup_dropped.reasoning: Company promised a callback to schedule follow-up work and then ghosted the customer.

Immediately he diagnosed the issue was that the water heater was beyond its warranty period and showing signs of needing to be replaced. Sat-Sun, same...nadda.  Monday morning started ok  I checked the Cinch site and still nothing was in their system of the diagnosis.  I called Lucky's and they said it could be because the service call was Friday and that could be the issue.  When I corrected them and told them the service call was not Fri but Thu, he held to the same reasoning.  I called Cinch and they said they would reach out to the repair company.  Shortly after talking with them the water heater failed and flooded my garage.  I'm glad we were home. I called Cinch on Tuesday and they assured me they would get the acceptance and approval of the repair sent to Lucky's. Finally on Thur, they said they could get me on the schedule for Mon!  Friday morning (today), I get a text that they could come out today if I'm available.  Of course I am.  I got a notification at 1250 that the repairman was en route.  TWO hours later, he was not on site and no information as to the hold up from a local repair person but that was par for the course since it was the same thing on the first time he came out.  There's more but I'm tired of talking about it, honestly.  It may be that I'm just unlucky.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but my experience with Jim McDonald & Sons Heating & Cooling was frustrating enough that I feel obligated to share it. Hopefully, this helps someone else avoid the same experience.

On Friday evening, my HVAC unit stopped running due to a clogged drain line. I called the office and spoke with Chelsea, who was helpful and quoted me $238 ($200 cash price) for a technician to come out, inspect the unit, and clean the drain line if that was the issue. Based on that quote, I scheduled the service.

Paul arrived within an hour, which I appreciated. After inspecting the unit, drain line, and coils, he confirmed the drain line was clogged and agreed that the cost would be the quoted $200 cash price. Based on that understanding, I authorized the work.

While clearing the drain line, Paul pointed out some sawdust buildup in an adjacent area (see attached photo). He used a handheld shop vacuum to remove the debris from an area approximately 12" x 24" and vacuumed as far as he could reach by hand. At no point was I informed there would be an additional charge for this work, nor was I asked to approve any additional service. The vacuuming took roughly 20 minutes.

Only after the work was completed did Paul call the office to determine what to charge. He then returned with a bill for $400—double the agreed-upon amount. In other words, I was charged an additional $200 for approximately 20 minutes of vacuuming in a very small area. Had I been told beforehand that this would cost an additional $200, I would have declined the service immediately and completed it myself. I understand this service being a small incremental amount, but $200 caught me off guard.

I paid the bill but informed Paul that I would be contacting the office to discuss the unexpected charge.

On Sunday, I spoke with Chelsea again. She was understanding of my concerns and told me the owner, Bob, would contact me on Monday. By 12:30 PM Monday, I still had not heard from him, so I called the office. No one answered. Less than five minutes later, Bob called me back.

Unfortunately, that conversation only created more confusion. Bob provided an explanation that differed from what both Chelsea and Paul had told me. He stated that the $400 charge included a diagnostic and trip charge. Given the conflicting explanations, I requested an itemized invoice.

The invoice only reinforced my concerns. See attached photo of description of work. The drain-line cleaning was listed at $238, despite the fact that I paid the quoted $200 cash price. While that discrepancy may seem minor, it highlights the larger issue I experienced throughout this process: inconsistent communication, unclear pricing, and charges that did not align with what was discussed before the work was performed.

What makes this even more concerning is that on May 1, 2026, the company posted on Instagram that "McDonald Home Services keeps things simple with no extra charges after hours and diagnostic fees covered when you move forward with repairs. Flexible financing makes bigger fixes easier to handle without the stress." A copy of that post is attached.
That statement directly conflicts with both my experience and the itemized invoice I was provided. I was charged fees beyond what was originally quoted, and the invoice clearly includes a diagnostic charge that was not waived despite moving forward with the repair.

My frustration is not that I had to pay for service. My frustration is that I was charged for work that contradicts with the information provided. Transparent pricing and customer authorization should be standard practice, especially when homeowners are dealing with urgent repairs.

I will also be submitting this information to the Better Business Bureau so that others can make an informed decision.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Customer was quoted $200, then billed $400 including an unapproved extra charge and a diagnostic fee the company advertises as waived.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: He then returned with a bill for $400—double the agreed-upon amount

frontline_communication.snippet:
LOOK ELSEWHERE!!!! ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE!!!!

We have spent a year dealing with this company and can’t begin to describe their incompetence and immorality.
Our saga began a year ago with a full system install (2 Daikin Fit units + ductwork). The units have not worked correctly the entire time we have owned them.  We have had at least 20-30 service calls without any relief. We are continually several degrees off from the set temperature with humidity of 70% and above.
The workmanship provided by this company is shockingly substandard (see photo album). When running a lineset, they took a sledgehammer unnecessarily to my flower bed, destroying it. The course of the lineset was above ground for several feet at both ends which looked laughably unsightly. When asked to come fix it, their tech took rocks from my drainage culvert and scrap pavers from my garage and piled it up over the lineset (see photo album). The lineset cover was applied crooked and any gaps were filled with spray foam.
We have recently had 2 independent inspections done of the units from reputable local companies. Both concluded that the ductwork is undersized and the upstairs unit is critically overfilled with coolant. Due to the insufficient air supply, my units will never function appropriately as designed.
Unfortunately, due to prolonged exposure to dangerously high humidity from underperforming units and inappropriately sealed ductwork penetrations, my home now suffers from multiple areas of mold growth which are affecting my family’s health and well-being (see photos).
Bob’s offer to remedy my situation was to switch out my units at an additional cost of $9500 to ME!! He will look you in the face and tell you that everything is working as intended despite having never seen your home/system. I’ll let the photos speak for themselves.
We are unfortunately proceeding with litigation against this company. There are far better A/C companies to do business with in Sarasota (check out AAP air or AC Today which are amazing). We regret the day we ever called Jim McDonald and sons. BEWARE!!!!

service_quality_in_session.snippet:
I had a very disappointing experience with Family Comforting and Air through my home warranty company. I originally contacted my warranty company because I noticed watermarks forming on my bathroom wall and on the ceiling directly beneath the AC unit area. They dispatched this company to inspect the issue.

The technician spent less than five minutes looking at the system. He briefly checked the drip pan, acknowledged that it was rusty, but quickly dismissed it by saying “it’s not that bad.” The drip pan is located directly above the exact area where the water damage is appearing, yet he insisted the issue had nothing to do with the AC and told me to “check the roof.”

To be thorough, I hired a roofing professional afterward, who confirmed the roof was not the cause of the watermarks near the AC unit. This made the inspection from Family Comforting and Air feel rushed, dismissive, and incomplete.

What made the experience even more uncomfortable was the way the technician pushed for a five-star review before leaving. He asked me to pull out my phone, sent me the review link himself, and heavily guided the process to the point where it felt inappropriate and pressured.

When I later called the company to follow up and express my concerns, I was talked over on the phone and made to feel like my concerns did not matter. Instead of listening to me as a homeowner and customer, the technician stated that we were “not understanding each other,” rather than addressing the actual issue.

From my experience, it felt more important to close out the warranty claim quickly and secure a positive review than to properly diagnose the problem. That process feels unethical, especially when homeowners rely on these companies for honest assessments and repairs.

I cannot recommend this company based on my experience.
service_quality_in_session.reasoning: Technician gave a rushed, cursory inspection that the customer found incomplete.
service_quality_in_session.quote: The technician spent less than five minutes looking at the system

frontline_communication.snippet: I could not be more disappointed with this company. They installed a brand new HVAC unit for the previous homeowners last year. Shortly after buying the house mold began growing on the supply box of the indoor unit. I had another company come out who informed me that the unit was not installed correctly and we were losing air all around the supply box causing condensation and mold. They recommended having the installer (Air it Cool) come out to fix their mistake since rebuilding the supply box would be about $600. When I finally got them out here, they did a sloppy job and it still has condensation and water running down the front of the unit. Right after they left, the unit stopped working completely. We called them and they refused to come back out without charging me and it wouldn’t have even been same day. I was told “just because we touched it last, doesn’t mean we broke it”. Umm yea you did. I was then called “an uneducated homeowner” because I didn’t know where the drain is on the system. So unprofessional and rude. I had to have another company come out that night and do an emergency visit because it was 86° in my house and climbing. The second company informed me that due to fixing some of the air leak, it changed the static pressure in my system which allowed water to back up in the safety switch. They repositioned the drain pipes so there was a trap to prevent that from happening. Took them about 10 minutes and they were so kind and professional. I will still have to pay someone to come out and properly fix the condensation problem. Air it Cool should have stood behind their work and offered to come out and assess the problem they clearly caused instead of attempting to make me feel bad that I am not an HVAC professional and shift blame. DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY. Shoddy work and absolutely rude.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Reviewer describes the staff's tone and behavior as rude and unprofessional, including calling her 'an uneducated homeowner'.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
Lew Miesz worked on our very old and battered AC unit at a prior residence and was so wonderful that when we finally purchased our next home, we couldn’t think of a better person to call for service.
Addendum-
It upsets me to write this. We used Miesz Mechanical in 2014-2016 and when we bought again in 2019, we, of course, stuck with Lew. Lew is very nice and so is his employee Danny. We have two units, one upstairs and one down. The upstairs unit became problematic in May of 2021. Danny came out and provided a quote for the work, which we agreed to. A week later, when the work was completed, the payment was $100 more. I did not realize it at the time but went back to compare and there it was. I attempted to contact Miesz for an explanation and it took several weeks to finally get one. Fast forward to 6/27/22. Our upstairs unit was making a noise and not cooling. From past experience, we thought it was likely the condenser fan. We were told there would be an overtime fee totaling $230 to come out. We were also told to turn off the unit. We decided to wait until the next Tuesday, to avoid the extra fee. They came out and could not replicate the problem and told us that everything seemed to be running normal. On 7/3/22 we came back from a short vacation to a hot upper level and that same sound coming from the machine. We had family in town and had to pay the extra fee for them to come out the same day. No one stepped foot inside my home to check on things, nor did anyone go into the attic to check on the handler. We were told it was the condenser fan and were charged nearly $1K for the replacement. It was still not cooling upstairs and by 7/13/22 it was not getting under 81 degrees during the day, with the unit running. We called again and were advised that the handler needed replacing and that the outside unit looked pretty good. We were told that we would have an estimate within a day or two. I was charged $260 for the visit, just to tell me that I need a new handler.  So I am now out nearly $1500 for essentially a condenser motor. I am 6 days out with no estimate and not even a call to let me know that there is a delay. I have called several other providers- whom do not charge overtime rates and have provided me with estimates within 24 hours. Customer service is clearly NOT a priority for Miesz and, unfortunately, I will not be using them again.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Agreed to a quote but the final payment was $100 higher than quoted, discovered after the fact.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: the payment was $100 more

⭐☆☆☆☆

Very disappointing experience.

When we first moved to Apollo Beach two years ago, we hired Knights Air Conditioning because several neighbors recommended them. Initially, everything seemed fine and the service appeared professional.

Last year, we had an issue with our HVAC system and were told repairs would cost around $3,500. Strangely, after the technician left, the system started working again and we never received any meaningful follow-up.

This year, when our AC stopped blowing cold air, we called them again. The technician inspected the system and told us the outside unit was “operating at 60%” and that the compressor was likely failing. We were quoted approximately $7,000 for repairs or around $11,500 for a new unit. At no point were we given a clear recommendation or a simple troubleshooting approach. Meanwhile, we still had no AC.

The next day, we decided to get a second opinion from another company. Within about 10 minutes, their technician identified the actual problem: a blown capacitor. They replaced the capacitor Fl which they carried in their work truck for $150, and within 20 minutes our AC was working perfectly again and cooling the home.

That experience completely changed my view of this company. What Knights Air Conditioning presented as a potential $7,000–$11,500 issue ended up being a simple $150 repair.

Based on my experience, I no longer feel confident that they were looking out for our best interests. I strongly recommend homeowners get a second opinion before agreeing to major HVAC repairs or replacement recommendation from this company.

frontline_communication.snippet: Supported this locally owned business for years, and will never use again after a particularly poor service experience. They came to service our home AC units as part of our bi-annual agreement in July. A week later we noticed our upstairs unit was not keeping temp during hot afternoons, and we called them back to check it out for us. Took a few days but a tech returned, looked it over, told us he couldn’t find a problem and charged us a service fee. All good, we’ll see what happens. The problem persisted so we called again, and again a few days later a tech returned, completed some service but found no issues. We continued to have issues and having already had techs out twice and with a newborn in the house, I finally reached out to the owner. He reluctantly came over, making it well known he was there against his wishes. He was extremely condescending to us telling us the issue was our thermostat settings (which hadn’t been changed at any point) or our air filter (which was admittedly dirty, but hadn’t been checked in other service calls!). He didn’t actually check our unit at any point, and he drove away with a laugh as I told him the temperature upstairs had gone up a degree since he arrived. Again, our son was 3 months old at the time, in the middle of the summer in Florida. We finally switched to another HVAC company, and surprise, the issue was not our filter. I’m sure many have had great experiences, but as for us, McWilliams has lost our business for good.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Owner was dismissive and condescending in tone toward the customer.
frontline_communication.quote: He was extremely condescending to us

booking_friction.snippet: We were originally recommended this company from a friend. We've been trying to have our AC blower motor replaced through them for over a month now and it only just got done as of today. First, we called to schedule a diagnosis we were told would be free. I spoke to 2 different Secretaries and was assured we were on the route list for the upcoming week. Me and my wife both took off work, only for no one to show up. No call/text/email confirmation either. We called a couple days after and somehow we were never added to their schedule at all. So we rescheduled and my wife took off work again. Once they were actually able to come out and give us a diagnosis, they tried to charge my wife when Martin told us it would be free, which isn't the technicians fault, but instead, poor communication on the management side with their employees. Then, our part had to be ordered. It took over 2 weeks to come in, and once it did and the technician was finally able to come back out, he had a mishap trying to install it and our new part was damaged. So after the part being ordered AGAIN and me and my wife wife having to call out of work AGAIN, we asked for a 50 dollar cash discount on the 650 dollar service charge, which I believe to be reasonable for the inconvenience and missed work time this has caused us - but we were denied that. It's like a slap in the face for all of their mistakes that they themselves could've avoided from happening. frontline_communication.snippet:
I would not recommend Polar Ice Air.

My experience was extremely frustrating from start to finish. After providing an estimate and moving forward with the project, the company later attempted to increase the price before work even began. This came after previous mistakes and delays related to the order, which had already cost valuable time.

What disappointed me most was the lack of professionalism and communication. Instead of a phone call to discuss the situation, I received a text message informing me that the price increase was "non-negotiable." As a customer, I expect transparency, accountability, and direct communication when issues arise.

Matthew was particularly rude, dismissive, and inconsiderate of both my time and my wife's time throughout this process. We rearranged our schedules, waited on updates, and tried to be patient while issues were addressed, only to be met with poor communication and an apparent lack of concern for the inconvenience being caused.

I entered this project in good faith based on the agreed-upon estimate. Being asked to absorb additional costs due to circumstances that appeared to be the company's responsibility was unacceptable. Rather than taking ownership of mistakes and delays, the burden was shifted to the customer.

Do not use this company. Get everything in writing, and be prepared for the possibility that the price you agree to may not be the price you're later asked to pay. Based on my experience, I would strongly caution anyone considering hiring them.

Unfortunately, this experience left me with little confidence in the company's reliability, professionalism, customer service, or respect for their customers' time.

Update to Company Response

Unfortunately, your latest message only reinforces the concerns I have expressed from the beginning. While you continue to explain why the delays, cost increases, and project issues occurred, you still refuse to take responsibility for them.

As the customer, I hired your company—not your suppliers. Any issues with suppliers, pricing, availability, or project management ultimately fall under your responsibility. Those are risks that should be anticipated and managed by the contractor, not passed on to the customer after an estimate has been accepted and weeks of delays have already occurred.

What stands out most is the complete lack of accountability. Rather than acknowledging the impact your decisions and project management had on your customer, every response attempts to redirect responsibility elsewhere. Being accountable is just as important as doing quality work. When problems arise, customers want to work with companies that own mistakes, communicate openly, and take responsibility for the outcome.

Instead, your responses have consistently focused on explaining why none of this was your fault. That may be your position, but it is not one I agree with.

Customers should be wary of doing business with any company that refuses to accept responsibility when things go wrong. The way a company handles mistakes and setbacks says far more about its professionalism than how it handles projects when everything goes according to plan.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer describes Matthew's tone as rude and dismissive throughout the process.
frontline_communication.quote: rude, dismissive, and inconsiderate

booking_friction.snippet:
If there less 1 star i will do !

In August 2023, my air conditioner stopped cooling. I contacted "Ken hope," a company recommended to me by the home's previous owner, who had been a regular client of theirs.
He had informed me that the AC units were under warranty and that we needed to transfer the coverage into my name.
A technician arrived and explained that the AC's drainage line was clogged and required cleaning. He performed the work, left me with a $100 invoice, and departed.
The AC resumed working for only two nights before breaking down again—bear in mind that this unit serves the bedrooms, and it was August, meaning scorching summer heat, and I have children! I called the company again to report the issue, but they scheduled me for an appointment a month later.
I told the representative that I could not wait a month—that it involved the bedrooms, I had children, and the weather was sweltering.
Her response was simply that I was not a "regular customer" and, because I was a new client, no earlier appointments were available for me!
I asked her if she was serious, and she replied, "Yes." She then demanded that I pay the outstanding $100 balance from just two days prior, which I refused to do due to her unprofessional attitude.
A year later, I called again to transfer the warranty into my name because the other AC unit required repairs. They told me, "You have no warranty coverage," and rejected my request.
The technician I currently work with also called them on my behalf, and they refused once again! This is, without a doubt, the worst company to deal with.
booking_friction.reasoning: Urgent AC failure met with a next appointment a month out.
booking_friction.quote: they scheduled me for an appointment a month later

frontline_communication.snippet:
3/14/2024
Beware of Carrier
We are in Sun City Center Florida.  Shortly after buying this house we had new HVAC unit installed.  That was 3 years ago.  A heat pump and air handler combo from Carrier.  Installed by Caldeco.  Told it was a good brand and good unit.  It was not the top of line but not the cheapest either. This Carrier unit has had problems from the beginning.  We have had about a dozen service calls.  It seems like 50 but 12 is about right.  One service call was a clogged drain which was on me.  I learned Florida requires different maintenance than Ohio. The balance were for 2 seemingly unrelated problems.  One is the heat pump unit was not shutting off and a literal block of ice was forming in the air handler around the coils and cold air was falling out of the intake vent.  It took several service calls to get that one figured out and it was my Wife pointing out to them that it never shuts off to get them to check the right thing.  So it was eventually fixed, or at least that is what we thought.  The second one is that occasionally there is a loud squeal /grinding noise when the air handler kicks in.  Several calls to fix this one also.  The blower has been replaced.  The noise still happens we just got sick of rearranging our schedule for yet another service call so we live with the occasional noise.  We have put up with this with no public bitching but the latest is just too much.
A week ago we noticed, hard not to, that we were getting air blowing but it was not cool.  Turns out the heat pump was not running.  One more service call.  Heat pump is not running because there is no coolant in the lines.  There is no coolant because the coils have a leak.  Those same coils that were repeatedly frozen in a solid block of ice, expanded and contracted.  Caldeco reps (2) say that is the likely cause of the leak.   Caldeco is of course no help.   They are “just the installer”.  Passing the buck is alive and well.  We have been with out AC for a several days waiting for the replacement coils and are being charged $1380 for the repair and just short of $300 for the service call.  For a unit that is about 1/5 of its expected life span.

4/14/2024
All the above was sent to both parties a month ago.  Zero action.  It seems doubtful they care at all.  Customer service is just too much trouble.  We all need AC in Florida.  Spend your money with someone else.
