billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
Called for emergency AC repair after hours.   Steve came out and repaired the AC quickly! He came from Plant City to Lakeland--and fast. We thought we were going to have to stay at a hotel because it was going to be a timely repair but it literally took him 20 minutes to fix.  Would definitely recommend for FAST and professional service.

EDIT TO ADD:  He sat and waited for me to write my review before telling me my price which was VERY expensive.

FINAL EDIT:
The Air Cool A/C Technician from Plant City, Steve, showed up after normal business hours to repair a water leak at the Air Handler. He fixed the water leak, but gave no indication of the cost involved. After the repair, he asked if I would give him a good review on Google. He waited while the review was done. When he was satisfied that a stellar review was posted, he let me know that the cost was $557 for 25 minutes of work. He did not give me an estimate of cost, and never advised me of his after-hour rates. He also did not write paid on the invoice after charging my credit card. The next day, the property manager was notified who then said they wouldn't cover the cost. They called Steve to see why the cost was so high and he lied to them and said he was there 2 hours! They said they then looked him up on the BBB and saw complaints against him. I called Steve to see if he would lower the bill because it was, after all, excessive. He said, "if you adjust my review I will take the cost down to $350." I no longer feel this company can be trusted. The fact that he waited to give me the invoice until he got a good review from me is an underhanded business practice. Most customers needing a/c repairs will check his reviews and call for service, not realizing that he is tricking them into giving good reviews, then charging excessive costs. To people thinking of using this man for after-hours work, I do not recommend him. He price gouges.   If you so choose to go with him-just be prepared to pay a lot of money.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: No estimate or rate disclosure before an expensive after-hours charge, a clear surprise-billing case.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Went in to ask for an estimate, since I want to replace my condos AC, and since I’m between jobs and worked for a contractor for 7 years, I thought I’d hand in my resume in case they needed some office support.

Before I could finish my sentence, the older lady behind the desk cut me off with “NO”

Caught off guard I started to ask if they worked out in Tampa, and she must have thought I was asking about a job again, and cut me off mid-sentence with “NO!”

So I thanked her and left.

I worked for a contractor for seven years, and I have never been that rude to a walk in before… whether they were dropping off a résumé or looking for an installation…

The proper thing to do is to say “we aren’t hiring at the moment, but I’ll keep it on file in case anything changes“ and then take the résumé and let the person be on their way… or in my case, ask for an estimate… FYI.

I will be going with a nicer service provider to install my AC. Since I couldn’t even ask them for an estimate. And she just lost her contractor a cash job.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Front-desk staff was dismissive and rude to a walk-in customer, cutting them off mid-sentence.
frontline_communication.quote: the older lady behind the desk cut me off with “NO”

frontline_communication.snippet:
DO NOT use this company. Father & Sons was the third company I called out to give me an estimate to fix my AC. They were the only company that charged me for the estimate ($110), but I was willing to pay it for a detailed take from an honest family company on what's going on. The guy showed up, spent six minutes out by my AC testing my freon levels, then told me it'd cost me nearly $200 more for him to diagnose anything else to give me a proper estimate. He was not particularly friendly and did not make any effort to thoroughly explain what was going on. He was at my house for less than ten minutes and for $110, I left with zero information that could help me make a decision about what to do.

For reference, the first company (Quick Air USA) that came didn't charge at all for the estimate, and spent a solid half hour investigating the system and even took photos to show me and explain everything. They were very friendly and patient. The estimate from Father & Sons was also $800 higher than the other company's estimate. I was recommended Father & Sons by a friend, but I will absolutely not be using them.

When I tried to call explaining that perhaps we had had a misunderstanding and requesting a refund for the service call, the owner was incredibly rude with me on the phone, talking over me and not caring about my experience at all. I would hate to give these people more money to actually fix a problem and then hope they cared if something went wrong. I got zero sense of goodwill from anyone involved.

I highly, HIGHLY recommend looking elsewhere.

--

UPDATE to address their response: I, too, have a reference of exactly when the technician was here. He arrived at 4:12pm, gathered his things from his truck until about 4:20, spent a few minutes out by my unit, told me it'd cost more to diagnose anything, I paid him the $110, and then he left my house at 4:31pm. Even including his time gathering his things from his truck, that's less than 20 minutes. The company is flat-out lying in their response. Do not trust these people.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
We chose this guy for the job because he was referred by someone on New Port Richey Chat facebook.  We checked him out from the Nextdoor site and also from Yelp before deciding to use him.
The agreement was we bought the supplies, and paid him labor. We agreed on $2000.00 for the labor.  When he took the deposit, which was 35% = $700, he kept telling us that his merchant account got kicked back and kept coming to us 2 more times to get the same $700 deposit.
He told us that the job would be scheduled for Thursday and Friday.  Thursday came and he didn't do any work.  On Friday, he didn't show up until 1pm, worked till midnight.  Saturday he came to work half day and still did not get it done.
To date, 8/8/2024, he has been ghosting us since! We made several attempts to request him to report to work but were unsuccessful.
Upon calling the building permit department, we found that the permit had been filed but not paid while we had already paid a 35% deposit for the company to pull the permit and to start the work.
We then found out that he charged the deposit 3 times. Our credit card had 3 different transactions $2121 in total which he lied and told us that the merchant account had a problem, needed to rerun the deposit transaction!
Not only that he added a few more installation supplies and took them with him, never return our supplies which cost us $241.31
We already reported him to the FL licensing board and disputed our credit card. We are now left with the AC halfway installed!!!
Please anyone, we are posting here to let you know DO NOT use this guy; He is a crook, doesn't matter if he had a good review or referrals in the past, they maybe just worked together to scam people!!!
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Customer's card was charged the deposit three times, a clear double/multiple-charge payment error.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: 3 different transactions

calls_unanswered.snippet: This company was given our business by our home warranty.  Initially, everything was fine.  They even came out on a Sunday to do a call.  The technician, who later told me he was the owner, gave us the rundown of what happened and everything seemed fine.  Unfortunately, our claim was denied by the home warranty.  However, after discussing it with our home warranty, it was authorized.  The company's business/office manager called me soon after this authorization.  He offered me a "discount" to do AC maintenance on our system for about $375 in addition to repairing a blower.  (The initial quote, after the claim was denied was $450, from this company.)  I asked him to let me think about it but wanted to schedule our blower repair.  He said he would call me back after talking to the technician.  I never got a callback.  I called them five times the next morning (spread throughout) and never got a call.  So, I called my home warranty company, because it felt like my calls were being ignored.  They made contact with the company and said that they were waiting on a part to come in and then would call to set this appointment up.  That seemed odd to me (why couldn't they just answer or return my call?).  After I got off with the home warranty company, I decided to call one more time.  This time, the owner/technician answered.  He was clearly frustrated that I had called the warranty company and said he was waiting on them to approve something.  All I wanted was to get an estimate on when the part would be in so the AC could be repaired.  He continued to gaslight me and belittle my concerns about communication; this is when he identified himself as the owner.  Confusion continued, and he eventually said he was refusing the work.  I don't profess to know everything (or anything) about AC systems.  So much of this may have been legitimate, but I felt confused and felt like there was some shadiness going on.  They seemed all too happy to fix my AC when they thought they could upsell me on an additional service.  When we cooled to that offer is when the service declined.  It felt manipulative.  The owner had every opportunity to explain the situation, if there was an explanation and chose not to.  He now is refusing to do the work, which means a new claim process has to be initiated and it's putting me out of additional service call money.  This seems unprofessional at best and manipulative at worst.
calls_unanswered.reasoning: Customer called five times seeking a promised callback and received none.
calls_unanswered.quote: I called them five times the next morning (spread throughout) and never got a call

frontline_communication.snippet:
EnviroAir Systems, came recommended to us by another company we were working with. We were hesitant to try them as we wanted to get a quote for specific work, but they would only provide a quote after coming by and doing a "detailed" inspection at the cost of $345. I have yet to find another professional business that charges to provide a quote. Given the recommendations and the small cost saving, we decided to proceed with Tampa Air Systems to have our 2 systems in our new house worked on to sanitize and remove mold. This was part of a bigger remediation project. We were quoted a further $6425 (plus the $345 already paid), so a total of $6770 for the work. For this, we expected the job to be done well! Seems like a lot of money to clean a system (no new parts). We also expected that Christopher would be doing the work since we were told he operated on his own.
We were out of state while the work was being completed and it turned into the biggest nightmare. Within the first couple of days of work, they had managed to break the blower while trying to remove it to clean it (the system is less than 5 years old). They called us up with the "bad news" to let us know it would cost us a further $600-900 to replace and that the part wouldn't come in for about a week. Meanwhile, it was hot and humid and only half the house had any A/C running, while the other half of the house had a heat producing massive dehumidifier and we were supposed to move in in a few days.
Christopher and his team missed many areas of mold and his work failed the mold recheck the first 2-3 times. He claims he wasn't responsible for cleaning the mold on the outside of AC ducting, yet it was part of the HVAC remediation plan supplied by a company he supposed works with often. In the end our general remediation contractor jumped in to keep things moving. We then had to have another area rechecked, and it turned out he had missed another section of mold on the HVAC system. We arrived in the middle of the night to a home that was about 90 degrees due to the HVAC system not operating and a dehumidifier still running. A day or two later, the part arrived and Christopher got it installed. He decided not to charge us for the blower, but all in all, at this point, we were super unhappy, frustrated and felt that the whole experience was terrible! But, at least it was rectified and complete. Or so we thought.
Within a few days of the work being completed, we couldn't understand why our upstairs unit was always running and never getting below 78/80 degrees. We could feel some cool air coming through the vents, but we could not get the upstairs cool. We had guests in town so put the concern aside as we were super busy, then started looking around. We found that while working on the handler in one of the units, the tape sealing the ducting and handler was coming off and half of the cool air was blowing into the HVAC closest. It was working just fine, but only some of the air was making its way into the ducting and the rest was freezing the utility closet. We reached out to Christopher with photos and texts and asked for this to be resolved - he was the only person to have worked on the unit or to have been in the closet and we had just paid almost $7K. He responded that this was not his concern. When we asked how that could be due to the service, inspection and work completed, he continued to deny any responsibility and got defensive. When we asked what we had actually paid for, he claimed that my husband was being aggressive (by asking this question) and refused any further work!
All in all, the experience was terrible, the follow through was missing and this company does not stand by their work. If you do decide to work with this company, make sure EVERY part of the work you would like completed is noted on the proposal or they will claim it isn't in their scope. Better still, find a different company and save yourself the headache! Previously posted on their old company name, but we paid to THIS company so it seems appropriate to share here.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer raised a specific concern about cool air venting into the closet and the provider dismissed it as not his concern.
frontline_communication.quote: He responded that this was not his concern.

delivery_quality.snippet:
Thunder Bay Air was hired by the former owner of our home to repair and replace old & damaged HVAC duct work throughout the house. They were also hired by the former owner to replace the AC unit. All of this work was done at our request as part of the addendum to the home sale. Thunder Bay Air was at our home a total of 3 times. First time they put in a new AC unit, then a new return duct under the house. Finally, they repaired two small sections of damaged metal duct work in the attic.

Since their involvement and our ownership of the house, we have discovered that the new unit was not installed properly, not hurricane clamped, not properly secured to the house, and the heat element was faulty. The new duct work under the home had to be secured and clamped to the foundation, as they simply left it lying on the ground, blowing around under the house.
The repairs to the duct work in the two attics had to all be torn out and completely replaced because the repair job was so poorly done, not only did it ruin the old ducts beyond further repair, but damaged our insulation so badly that  the insulation also had to be removed and replaced. Furthermore, his crews left 5-6 bags of trash throughout our attic & crawl space and 4-5 under the house.

When the owner of the company, Sam Beard, was confronted about the problem, and given a chance to visit our home to see the work of his crew, his response was that yes the work was "deplorable", and he would like to send the same crew to, "teach them a lesson". He also thought it would be acceptable to us that he "might get to it in 2-3 weeks".

The owner, of this company, Sam Beard, does not seem to have an actual HVAC background or skills, his website touts his work as an airline mechanic! After his company ruined our HVAC system, we had 6 different companies come look at their work, all recommended that the work was so badly done and beyond any further repair. He did not seem to have a response to this, and suggested that he could "maybe put some more mastic" and the gaping holes in our metal ducts. He did not properly acknowledge the horrible and shoddy work of his crew, and refused to take proper responsibility. As a result of this company, we had to spend and additional $7000 to have everything fixed!

Do not use this company!
delivery_quality.reasoning: The installed HVAC work was broken and did not meet spec, requiring full replacement.
delivery_quality.quote: the new unit was not installed properly, not hurricane clamped, not properly secured to the house, and the heat element was faulty

followup_dropped.snippet:
Please be aware that this company Mr No Sweat air conditioning and refrigeration is definitely not a reputable company.
A few months after Hurricane Helene in December of 2024 my air conditioning system started leaking and needed repairs on my system, my normal A/C company I used, performance air couldn't come out for 2 days which of course I couldn't wait so I called Mr Sweat, owner Richard Vierlingand came over to check out my unit. After a discussion with him I agreed to get a brand new unit since mine was over 14 years old and had storm damage. I looked up his company and his license and he was registered. Mr Vierling showed me on his lap top that he had submitted a permit on my behalf. There goes my first mistake. I had no reason at the time not to trust him. They came the following day and installed my unit. In June of 2025, I still waiting on my permit to come in. I called him and he said he would look into it. I knew the City of St Petersburg was slow in getting permits since it took over a year to get my home owners to repair my home after Helene.
I didn't get any call back after waiting 2 weeks. I then went to the permits office and found out he never submitted a petition at all. At which point I had to obtain a permit on my own for $69.00.
Since then I've been trying to reach out to him via text and phone call, no response.  I then called the city to come and check my unit for closure.
The inspector failed my permit from 6 separate deficiencies that Mr No Sweat failed to perform.
Since, Mr Vierling failed to respond to my emails and texts I sent certified mail to the 2 different address he had on his website. A week later they came back undeliverable.  I then called 2 other A/C companies to get a quote to repair those deficiencies, 2 quotes, one for $5,265.00 the other $3000.00 o top of the a/c I paid for which was $7800.00.
I was told by the city's inspector that I can't sell my home until these repairs are done.
This has been a very stressful time not only from the hurricane itself but also this company that like to take advantage of senior citizens like myself.
So before you go and spend your hard earned money. PLEASE, refrain from calling Mr No Sweat. Mr Vierling obviously has no integrity and refuses to help.
Look him up under court records.  You will see for yourself. Apparently I'm not the first but I hope I can help others not to make the mistake I did by hiring this incompetent company. If I could have given 0 stars I would have!!!

He hasn’t came back and I’ve left messages with him and called him several times to see when and what his plans were, he will not return my calls and he will not return my text. If there was something wrong I can understand if you tell me what the problem is but to ignore my text and my calls. I find a childish unprofessional and down mean I am on a time schedule here, and all I ask is the truth to be spoken by the individual who said that he would do the job. My suggestion is find someone else this individual does not have the professional courtesy to talk to the homeowner. Give them the real truth about what is going on, he is childish and unprofessional. You can’t do business with people like that because you never know where they’re coming from or if they’re telling you lies.
calls_unanswered.reasoning: Customer left messages and called several times but the contractor will not return the calls.
calls_unanswered.quote: I’ve left messages with him and called him several times to see when and what his plans were, he will not return my calls and he will not return my text
